rationale: The crawler landed on monclergroup.com, which is the corporate brand site and not the e-commerce PLP. This is a domain-level trap. The safest fix is to block monclergroup.com and rewrite any such hits to the store domain (moncler.com), then proceed to a category PLP. We avoid changing selectors to minimize risk and rely on robust PDP-anchor detection and canonical following to stabilize navigation.
code_hints: If current URL host ends with monclergroup.com or the page title/og:site_name contains 'Moncler Group', treat as a trap and immediately apply the rewrite to https://www.moncler.com/en.
After landing on moncler.com, if you are on the homepage, navigate to a category: click the first available nav link matching a[href^="/en/women"], a[href^="/en/men"].
From the category landing, open a PLP by clicking a subcategory link likely to list products, e.g. a[href*="/jackets"], a[href*="/ready-to-wear"], a[href*="/new-arrivals"].
Wait for a product grid by waiting for PDP anchors: a[href*="/en/"][href*="/products/"] (use this selector to collect product tiles and PDP links).
When collecting product cards on PLP, dedupe by href and constrain to visible elements within main or section elements.
On PDP, extract price using common fallbacks: [data-test*="price"], [class*="Price" i], [class*="price" i]. If none found, regex for currency symbols on the page as a last resort.
If no product anchors are found within a reasonable timeout on any page, follow rel=canonical if it points to moncler.com and retry once.
Set Accept-Language to 'en' to reduce geo/country gating and avoid region redirects. If still redirected to a locale-specific domain, continue as long as host remains moncler.com.
